sentences.text: Victoria’s Royal Commission into the Casino Operator and Licence examined whether Crown Melbourne was suitable to keep its casino licence and what action should follow.
sentences.support:
The Commission was established to inquire into, and report on, the suitability of Crown 
Melbourne to hold its casino licence.

sentences.text: The Commission found Crown Melbourne unsuitable and identified failures in legal compliance, corporate oversight and dealings with its regulator.
sentences.support:
When these facts came to light, it was inevitable that Crown Melbourne would be found 
unsuitable to hold its casino licence.

sentences.text: It recommended a Special Manager oversee the business for two years, followed by a regulatory decision on whether suitability had been restored.
sentences.support:
the Special Manager should be appointed to oversee 
and control its affairs for a period of two years.

sentences.text: Its 33 numbered recommendations cover regulatory powers, casino governance, money laundering controls and gambling harm, including mandatory limits on gaming-machine play.
sentences.support:
One recommendation is to make compulsory a pre-commitment system that imposes limits 
on time and money spent on gambling.

findings.quote:
When these facts came to light, it was inevitable that Crown Melbourne would be found 
unsuitable to hold its casino licence.

It is recommended that the Casino Control Act be amended to prohibit a casino 
operator from dealing with junket tour operators.

notes: The overview’s narrative and terms-of-reference answers occupy PDF pages 23–27; its recommendations and endnotes continue through PDF page 45. The total is taken from its numbered recommendations list. Findings from other inquiries are not independently attributed to this Commission.
